description: Comprehensive guide to choosing your first BJJ gi. Sizing, weave types, durability, and recommendations across price ranges.
intro_paragraphs: Choosing your first BJJ gi is a rite of passage. The wrong choice can mean a year of discomfort and expensive replacements.
This guide covers what to look for at each price point, sizing, and care.

items.text: Pearl weave is the standard — durable but breathable.
550-650 GSM for daily training; lighter for hot climates.
If you compete IBJJF, ensure the gi meets size and color rules.

items.title: Beginner ($60-100)
items.subtitle: First gi, learning durability needs
items.body: Hayabusa Goorudo, Sanabul Essentials. Reliable construction without breaking the bank.

items.title: Intermediate ($120-180)
items.subtitle: Daily training, year-round use
items.body: Tatami Estilo, Hyperfly ProComp. Better fabric, longer lifespan.

items.title: Premium ($200+)
items.subtitle: Competition + frequent training
items.body: Shoyoroll, Origin USA. Premium construction, long lifespan, often handmade in USA/Brazil.

items.text: Hot water shrinks BJJ gis significantly. Always cold wash.
Dryer heat is the #1 killer of gis. Hang dry every time.
1 cup white vinegar in the wash kills bacteria without bleaching colors.

faq.question: How many gis do I need?
faq.answer: Minimum 2 — one to wash, one to wear. 3-4 if you train 4+ times per week.

faq.question: Are expensive gis really worth it?
faq.answer: Diminishing returns above ~$180. The biggest jump in quality is from $60 to $120.
